senses.definition: A part that opens or closes to control where liquid or gas moves.
senses.example: A valve in your heart closes to keep blood from moving backward.

senses.definition: A room or an enclosed space inside something.
senses.example: Each chamber in the heart holds blood for part of a heartbeat.

senses.definition: Movement around a place or along a path that brings something back again.
senses.example: The movement of blood around the body is called circulation.

senses.definition: One of the tiny air sacs in the lungs where gases move between air and blood.
senses.example: Oxygen can pass through the thin wall of an alveolus.

senses.definition: The broad muscle below your lungs that helps you breathe.
senses.example: The diaphragm moves down to make room for the lungs to fill with air.

senses.definition: The main tube that carries air from your throat toward your lungs.
senses.example: Air moves down your windpipe as you breathe in.

senses.definition: The way your body breaks food down into small parts it can take in and use.
senses.example: Chewing and mixing food with saliva start digestion.

senses.definition: The watery liquid your mouth makes to moisten food and start breaking it down.
senses.example: Saliva helps make a dry cracker easier to swallow.

senses.definition: The part of your body that holds food after you swallow it and mixes it with juices.
senses.example: Food moves from the stomach into the small intestine.

senses.definition: A long, folded tube in the body that helps take useful parts from food and carry along the rest.
senses.example: Your small intestine takes in most nutrients.

senses.definition: A substance that a living thing needs to grow, get energy, or stay healthy.
senses.example: Calcium is a nutrient that helps build strong bones.

senses.definition: The tube that carries swallowed food and drinks from the throat to the stomach.
senses.example: Muscles in your esophagus squeeze to move food toward your stomach.

senses.definition: One of the body parts that clean the blood and make urine from some waste and extra water.
senses.example: A kidney can return water to the blood after filtering it.

senses.definition: The liquid waste you pass when you pee.
senses.example: The kidneys make urine and send it to the bladder.

senses.definition: A stretchy pouch inside the body that holds urine until you pee.
senses.example: The bladder gets larger as it fills with urine.

senses.definition: Something that lets some parts of a mixture through and holds other parts back.
senses.example: A paper filter holds back the grains when water drips through.

senses.definition: To remove parts of a mixture by passing it through something.
senses.example: The kidneys filter small materials from the blood.

senses.definition: A tiny part of a kidney that filters the blood, then takes useful material back.
senses.example: Some water passes into a tube inside a nephron.

senses.definition: A nerve cell that carries a message in the body.
senses.example: A neuron can send a signal to another neuron.

senses.definition: A sign or message that tells what is happening or what to do.
senses.example: The bell was our signal to go inside.

senses.definition: To send someone a sign or message.
senses.example: We waved to signal that we were ready.

senses.definition: A thick bundle of nerve tissue protected by the backbone that carries many messages between the brain and body.
senses.example: Signals that help move your foot can travel through your spinal cord.

senses.definition: A thin layer of tissue in the ear that moves when sound reaches it.
senses.example: Air vibrations make the eardrum move slightly back and forth.

senses.definition: A curled part of the inner ear that helps change sound vibrations into signals the brain can use.
senses.example: Tiny hair cells in the cochlea move when waves pass through its liquid.

senses.definition: A muscle that can help move your body by pulling on a bone.
senses.example: A skeletal muscle in your upper arm helps bend your elbow.

senses.definition: A strong strip of tissue that joins a muscle to a bone or another body part.
senses.example: A tendon carries the pull from your calf muscle to your heel bone.

senses.definition: A muscle at the front of your upper arm that helps bend your elbow.
senses.example: Your biceps muscle works when you bend your elbow to lift a bag.

senses.definition: A muscle at the back of your upper arm that helps straighten your elbow.
senses.example: Your triceps muscle works when you push your hand away from your shoulder.

senses.definition: A way to name a number by telling how many equal parts of a whole you have.
senses.example: The fraction 3/4 means three parts when the whole is divided into four equal parts.

senses.definition: The top number in a fraction, showing how many of the equal-size parts are counted.
senses.example: In 3/4, the numerator is 3.

senses.definition: The bottom number in a fraction, showing how many equal parts make one whole.
senses.example: In 3/4, the denominator is 4.

senses.definition: Equal in value or meaning, even if shown in a different way.
senses.example: Two quarters and one half are equivalent amounts.

senses.definition: A line with marked spots showing where numbers are in order and how far apart they are.
senses.example: On a number line, 1/2 is halfway between 0 and 1.

senses.definition: The amount of flat space inside a shape.
senses.example: The area of the tiled floor is 24 square meters.

senses.definition: A particular part of a place.
senses.example: We ate in a shaded area of the park.

senses.definition: The distance all the way around the edge of a flat shape.
senses.example: Add all four side lengths to find the perimeter of a rectangle.

senses.definition: A flat shape with four straight sides and four square corners.
senses.example: A square is a rectangle whose four sides are all the same length.

senses.definition: Using only two choices, like the digits 0 and 1 in computer numbers.
senses.example: In binary counting, 10 means two.

senses.definition: A small piece or amount of something.
senses.example: There was a bit of icing left on the spoon.

senses.definition: A tiny unit of computer information that can be 0 or 1.
senses.example: Three bits can store one of eight different patterns.

senses.definition: A group of eight bits that a computer handles as a unit.
senses.example: A file with 100 bytes contains 800 bits.

senses.definition: A set of clear steps for solving a problem or doing a job.
senses.example: We followed an algorithm to find a name in the sorted list.

senses.definition: Something that has to be true for a rule or action to apply.
senses.example: Our game ends if one player reaches ten points. Reaching ten points is the condition.

senses.definition: How something is doing or what kind of shape it is in.
senses.example: The bicycle was old but still in good condition.

senses.definition: A trick where someone sends a message that looks real to get private information or get someone to do something unsafe.
senses.example: A grown-up helped us check whether the unexpected sign-in message was phishing.

senses.definition: A secret you enter to help prove that you are allowed to use something.
senses.example: We chose a password so other people could not sign in to our account.

senses.definition: A tool that stores and helps you use your passwords safely.
senses.example: With a trusted grown-up, we used a password manager to keep track of different passwords.

senses.definition: A place with a service or business where information about one person or group is kept.
senses.example: When I signed in to my library account, it showed the books I had borrowed.

senses.definition: A description of what happened.
senses.example: She gave her account of how the plant pot fell.

senses.definition: Something that connects two things, such as a ring in a chain or an item on a page that opens another page.
senses.example: I tapped the link to read about the Moon.

senses.definition: To join or connect things.
senses.example: We linked the paper rings to make a chain.

senses.definition: The point that a lever turns around.
senses.example: The support under the middle of a seesaw is its fulcrum.

senses.definition: A stiff bar that turns around a point and helps move something.
senses.example: A seesaw is a lever with a support under its middle.

senses.definition: A wheel with a groove along its edge that guides a rope or cable.
senses.example: The rope passed over a pulley so we could pull down to lift the flag.

senses.definition: Something being carried, lifted, or supported.
senses.example: The crane lifted a load of bricks.

senses.definition: To put something in or on something else so it can be carried or used.
senses.example: We loaded the wagon with books.

senses.definition: How high or low a sound seems.
senses.example: The whistle had a higher pitch than the drum.

senses.definition: To throw a ball toward someone who will try to hit it.
senses.example: We took turns pitching the ball during baseball practice.

senses.definition: A gas in air that your body needs, carried from the lungs by blood.
senses.example: When you breathe in, some oxygen enters your blood.

senses.definition: A gas whose molecules each contain one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms. You release some of it when you breathe out.
senses.example: Carbon dioxide moves from the blood into the air inside your lungs.

senses.definition: A push or pull that can change how something moves or change its shape.
senses.example: The force from my hand made the door swing open.

senses.definition: To make someone do something or make something move by using strength or pressure.
senses.example: The wind forced the door shut.
